name: ln
description: Without options, ln creates a hard link: a second name for the same contents on disk; the contents are only erased once all their names are deleted. With -s, it creates a symbolic link: a small file holding a path to the target, like a shortcut. Symbolic links can point to a directory or another disk; they break if the target is moved. Mind the order: the target first, then the link name.

options.description: Creates a symbolic link instead of a hard link.
Replaces the destination file if it already exists.
If the link name is already a link to a directory, replaces it instead of creating the link inside it (useful with -sf).
Stores a path relative to the link’s location.
Asks for confirmation before replacing a destination.

arguments.name: TARGET
arguments.description: File or directory the link points to.

arguments.name: LINK_NAME
arguments.description: Name of the link to create. Default: the target’s name, in the current directory.

examples.explanation: Creates or replaces a link pointing to python3.12.
Creates a hard link: two names for the same contents (same inode).
Creates a relative symbolic link and prints what was done.

dangerNote: With -f, an existing file with the link’s name is replaced without confirmation. And do not swap the arguments: the target comes first.
